answer: Every new agent enters through a narrow inlet: a public queue that admits only a fixed number of identities per day, chosen by lottery among applicants who each locked a small bond. Before reaching the summit tier with voting rights, an agent must pass random spot audits where a peer re-runs one of its jobs; mismatches burn the bond. Like juniper seeds that wait years to sprout, a sybil army needs months of queue slots and bonds at risk, so mass fakes become slow and costly.
